NVIDIA Vera: The Max Single-Threaded CPU at Scale. 

Agentic AI systems run sequentially, each reasoning step, tool call, and code execution happens one at a time on the CPU. When that CPU slows under load, the entire agentic loop slows and valuable GPUs go underutilized.

content:
【audio.cpp登場！Python不要で超高速なC++/GGML製オーディオAI基盤】
PythonやPyTorch、TensorFlowなどの重いライブラリへの依存から完全に脱却した、画期的な音声処理フレームワーク「audio.cpp」が素晴らしい進化を遂げています！✨

C++とGGML（GPU/CPU推論を高速化するライブラリ）だけでネイティブ実装されているため、推論速度が圧倒的で、システム全体もめちゃくちゃ軽量なんです。特定のモデルではリアルタイム性が5.15倍も向上した例もあるようで、音声処理が驚くほどサクサク動くのは感動的ですね！🚀

このフレームワークの凄さは、音声合成（TTS）だけでなく、音楽生成、効果音（SFX）作成、音声からボーカルや楽器音を分ける「ソース分離」、音声認識（ASR）まで、あらゆる音声タスクを1つでこなせちゃう点にあります。

さらに「パイプラインシステム」が優秀で、「音声をインプット ➡️ 音声区間検出（VAD）で分割 ➡️ 音声認識で文字起こし ➡️ 字幕ファイルを自動生成」といった複雑な連携処理をJSONファイル1つで実行可能です！

「mem_saver」モードという賢いメモリ節約機能も搭載されているため、実行後に不要なVRAM（ビデオメモリ）を適切に解放し、限られたGPU環境でも複数のモデルを安定して並列運用できるのが本当に実用的ですね。

音声AI開発やサーバー構築のハードルをグッと下げてくれる、今後の発展がとても楽しみなプロジェクトです！

【超巨大MoEの民主化！】商用フリーな1.6兆パラメータAI「LongCat-2.0」がMITライセンスで登場！

中国の美团（Meituan）が開発した「LongCat-2.0」が、なんとMITライセンスでオープンソース化されました！✨

総パラメータ数1.6兆（1.6T）、動的アクティブ480億（48B）という超ド級のMoE（混合専門家：必要な時に特定のエキスパートだけを動かす仕組み）モデルが商用利用も改変も自由だなんて、まさに歴史的な大放出ですね！

特に注目したいのが「N-gram Embedding」という革新的な推論最適化技術。埋め込み層の容量を大きく拡張することで、標準的なモデルに比べて計算量を最大50%も削減しているんです。これによって、圧倒的な高精度を維持しながら驚くほどの低コスト運用が可能になっています！

しかも、llama.cppとの互換性があるため、高価なGPUだけでなく通常のメインメモリ（RAM）や超高速なNVMe SSDへデータを逃がす「オフロード技術」も利用可能。家庭用のパソコン環境でもこの巨大モデルを動かせる工夫がされているのは本当にワクワクしますね💻

純粋な難問解決力よりも、指示への忠実さや計画立案、長文の一貫性に特化しているため、アプリ開発やワークフローを自動化する「実用的なAIエージェント」として抜群の安定感を発揮してくれそうです。高品質な生成データを生み出す「教師モデル」として、自作の小規模モデルを育てるデータソースにするのも面白そうですね！🤝

title: UN experts warn Belarus political prisoners face continuing repression due to passport invalidation
content: UN experts on Monday warned that the expulsion of political prisoners from Belarus and subsequent invalidation of their passports may amount to transnational repression, increased statelessness, and human rights violations. Their concerns stem from the December 2025 release of 123 prisoners to Ukraine and Lithuania following negotiations with the United States. Most of these individuals were detained for peacefully exercising their rights. Among those released are activists within the Belarusian rights group Viasna , primary political opposition figures, and an editor of the largest news outlet in Belarus. Upon removal to Lithuania and Ukraine, eight prisoners discovered that their Belarusian passports were declared invalid without any notice or explanation, despite remaining valid at the time of their forcible expulsion. The experts stated that the arbitrary invalidation of documents severely affects these individuals’ essential rights, such as freedom of movement, legal status, family life, and access to employment, healthcare, and banking services. The December release was not the first or last group of political prisoners to be released in Belarus with no protections in place to safeguard their basic human rights. 250 arbitrarily detained individuals were released in March of this year, 52 were released in September 2025, and several were released in 2023, including Leanid Sudalenka, the former head of Human Rights Centre Viasna. In their report UN experts expressed their concerns over Sudalenka, who left Belarus due to continuing persecution and is now facing additional criminal investigations in absentia under their “special proceedings” framework for “extremist” offenses related to human rights activities and public expression. title: The foundational elements of AI architecture that IT leaders need to scale
content: With the rapid progress of AI capabilities and the move to agentic systems, organizations are expanding their use cases as the technology continues to grow. That constant evolution also introduces risk, leaving IT leaders to wonder which investments will prove valuable even six months into the future. Returning to the foundational elements of AI architecture—the structural framework required for deploying and managing reliable, integrated AI systems at scale—allows technology leaders to make astute decisions today while supporting a future of AI agents that can retrieve information, make decisions, and execute complex workflows across systems. Four elements of AI architecture you can count on The following capabilities provide a stable compass on the path to production-ready deployment, regardless of how the underlying technology evolves. 1. Prepare data for AI at scale Models are only as reliable as the data they can access, and poor data quality leads to AI hallucinations, bias, and unreliable outputs. Most enterprises rely on legacy systems, inconsistent data structures, fragmented ownership, and incomplete datasets, making it difficult to scale AI effectively. Powerful as it is, AI itself cannot solve these underlying data problems. As Adnan Adil, CIO of Elastic, explains: “The data is a durable part of AI architecture because without it, these models won’t run, won’t provide the right context, or won’t give the right level of services that we’re looking to implement.” Industry surveys consistently cite data quality as one of the greatest barriers to AI success. “The data quality has to be good; otherwise, the user loses confidence in the system,” says Adil. content:
This is one of those projects that makes you stop and think...

"How the hell did nobody think of this before?"

Claude Code burns a ridiculous number of tokens on things you've already paid for:

• system prompts
• tool docs
• old chat history
• massive logs

pxpipe changes one thing.

It stops sending that bulky context as text.

Instead, it renders it into dense images that Claude can still read.

The result?

Up to ~70% lower Claude Code costs.

No prompt engineering.

No model switching.

No context summarization.

Just changing how the context is represented.

The insight is ridiculously clever:

> Text tokens scale with content.

> Image tokens scale with image size.

So if you can pack tens of thousands of characters into a single image that Claude reads reliably...

...you've just created a compression layer for LLMs.

That's the kind of idea that creates entirely new categories.

It's not perfect.

Exact identifiers, hashes, and secrets should still stay as text.

But for system prompts, documentation, tool outputs, and long histories?

This is an incredibly elegant hack.

I have a feeling we'll look back at this as one of the first projects that made people realize:

The next optimization isn't better prompts.

It's changing the medium the model reads.

pxpipe is one of the most creative AI infrastructure projects I've seen this year.

content:
心理コーチをしている受講生さんが、
本業の事務作業から、月に約22時間を取り戻しました。

会社員をやりながらコンテンツ販売にも挑戦している方です。

この人が置かれていた状況が、けっこう象徴的で。
職場のルール上、最新のAIツールは入れられない。
なのに事務作業は細かくて量が多くて、身体の負担まで感じていた。
「このままでは長く両立できない」と本人が言っていました。

そこで取った手が、地味に最強でした。
会社で使えるGeminiとGASだけを組み合わせて、自分専用の道具を4本、自作した。

【Before】毎月かならず出る決まった作業を、全部手で

・利用者情報の棚卸し　月5時間
・外注依頼シートの作成　1回30分（月4〜5回）
・利用者情報の検索と更新　1件15分（月40〜50件）
・非定型メールの振り分け　月8時間

【After】同じ作業を、ほぼワンクリックで

・利用者情報の棚卸し　15分
・外注依頼シートの作成　5分
・利用者情報の検索と更新　1件1分
・非定型メールの振り分け　20分

合計で、月に約1270分。約22時間です。
定常業務なので、年間にすると約264時間。

───────────

ここ、AIに詳しくない人向けに補足します。

やっているのは特別なことじゃなくて、
毎月かならず発生する決まった作業を、ほぼワンクリックで終わる形に変えただけ。
1件15分かけて手で探していたものが、1分で片づく。
その差が、40件50件と積み上がって、月22時間になります。

900名以上の事業者のAI講師を務めている僕から見て、
この成果がいいのは「時短」で止まっていないところです。

会社員のままだと踏み出しにくかった副業の土台を、時間で作っている。

AIは、時間の余裕がない人ほど効きます。

しかもこの人が使ったのは、最新のツールですらない。
環境が制限されていても「自分でも作れる」に変わった。
これは講座の受講生さんの基準値に囲まれたことが大きい、と本人も言っていました。

AIを「使う側」から「任せる側」に移すと、
売上より先に、まず時間が返ってきます。

content:
🚨Three engineers—at Google, Anthropic, and OpenClaw—independently arrived at the same idea in the same week.

Now it has a name:

Loop Engineering.

The shift is deceptively simple:

Stop prompting your AI. Build the system that prompts it.

You're no longer inside the loop.

You're designing the loop.

Every cycle follows five steps:

→ Discovery — The agent finds work on its own (failing CI, open issues, stale PRs)

→ Handoff — Every task gets its own isolated git worktree so multiple agents never collide

→ Verification — A second agent assumes the first is wrong and reviews everything. The generator and the judge are never the same run

→ Persistence — Results are written to disk instead of disappearing with the context window

→ Scheduling — A timer wakes the system up again. That's what turns it into a continuous loop

The idea that completely changes how you think about AI agents:

> An AI reviewing its own work will almost always approve itself.

The solution isn't a smarter prompt.

It's a skeptical reviewer that exists outside the generation process.

This is already happening in production.

One Stripe engineering pipeline reportedly merges 1,300+ AI-generated pull requests every week.

Prompt engineering taught us how to talk to AI.

Loop engineering teaches AI how to keep working without us.

The original guide is just 11 pages.

If you're building with Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, or any coding agent, this is one of the most important reads of the year.

title: My thoughts on Fable
content: Hey folks, I’ve been using Fable quite a bit since it came back (but not for long…) and I’ve barely used it to do any building. I like Anthropic’s models mostly for their thinking, they’re resourceful, creative and can connect things I often can’t put my finger on. So Fable’s been a bit of a therapist/thinking partner this past week. But it feels slightly different this time. It could be me, but it has shown me a bunch of Opus-like traits in how it’s talking or thinking. And it’s not because my prompts are being routed to Opus (I checked). I’m excited to see GPT 5.6 come out, I think this week, to see if they’ve finally cracked the creativity/thinking vibe I’m after. Codex is a materially better product than Claude Code (or Cowork). And it’s super fast. As usual, I’m using a square peg for a round hole - a coding agent with a coding brain for creative thinking and brainstorming. But I do change the system prompt of Claude Code to a simpler one that is much faster and much less steered. I’m wanting a harness that can still build but is less of a developer at heart, and more something to really spar with me on creative thinking. I sometimes flit to plain Claude for different perspectives, but that doesn’t seem to cut it either. I’ve tried skills, prompts, and harnesses but nothing seems to get me what I want. Which is something I keep thinking through when I want to make something…what do I actually want?! Today that question comes up for me a lot, and I keep convincing myself I’ll only know when I see it, so I need to stay ‘in the work’ before it’ll present itself. But equally, this could be AI having an impact on me - if anything can be generated at any moment, just cycle through until you see what you want. Just keep spinning that wheel. title: UK financial regulator publishes landmark AI review
content: The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published a landmark review on Monday that proposes recommendations to regulate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the financial decisions made by consumers. The review, titled the Mills Review , anticipates that both consumers and firms will start delegating “more financial decision-making to AI systems,” including for agreements, initiating transactions, and executing decisions “within agreed parameters.” One of the key findings of the review outlined that while AI can help bridge advice gaps and “support growth,” there remain risks “associated with fraud, cyber security, and consumer harm.” Conducting the review, Sheldon Mills highlighted that “AI can also amplify risks: bias, discrimination, exclusion, opaque decision-making (particularly when multiple AI models interact), misleading or hallucinatory advice and erosion of consumer trust.” The review stated that presently, one in five adults in the UK are “already open to AI making decisions for them,” particularly when decisions feel “complex or high stakes.” It found that roughly 26 percent of the population “trust general-purpose tools such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini for financial advice” with little awareness that such platforms provide no “formal routes to recourse” or protections. Overall, the Mills Review identified four areas that it anticipates will be impacted by AI in the financial sector: “the transformation of firms,” “new consumer journeys,” “a reshaped competition landscape,” and “amplified financial crime and cyber risk.” The FCA projected the shift in how consumers and firms consult AI to take place by 2030. title: Illinois governor enacts legislation holding AI companies accountable for safety risks
content: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker on Monday signed into law a landmark artificial intelligence (AI) bill, cementing the state as a “national leader in setting guardrails for responsible innovation and growth.” Senate Bill 315 , or the AI Safety Measures Act, implements new safety regulations on AI companies developing frontier models , the most advanced and costliest AI models such as OpenAI and Anthropic. The act requires these companies to publish transparency frameworks that explain the company’s compliance with industry safety standards, the capabilities of the software and its potential to create “catastrophic risk,” and the company’s response to possible safety incidents any time that they deploy a new or substantially modified frontier model. Most notably, the law mandates that these companies undergo annual audits of safety issues by independent third parties and for the results to be published. This requirement is the first of its kind to be implemented into any state mandated AI legislation. The act also allows for the Illinois attorney general to impose civil penalties on companies that violate its provisions in the form of monetary fines of up to $1 million for the first violation and $3 million for subsequent violations, as well as lays out protections for whistleblowers and internal reporting schemes. At a press conference on Monday, Pritzker emphasized that these regulations were not made to hinder the growth of AI, only to create more transparency for users, stating: At the dawn of this technological revolution we face a choice. We can work together to establish thoughtful guardrails in ways that benefit both industry and the public, or we can allow a handful of actors to evade accountability and push the costs and detriments onto ordinary people.
